title: Orally Administered 2-Oxo-Imidazole Dipeptides Exhibit Enhanced Stability and Distribution in the Brain and Kidneys of Mice and Hamsters
content: 2-Oxo-imidazole dipeptides (2-oxo-IDPs) are oxidized forms of imidazole dipeptides (IDPs) derived from food, which exhibit potent antioxidant activity and high resistance to carnosinase 1 (CN1). However, the oral absorption and tissue distribution of these compounds are unclear. Therefore, we examined the metabolic stability and tissue distribution of orally administered IDPs and 2-oxo-IDPs: carnosine, 2-oxo-carnosine, homocarnosine, and 2-oxo-homocarnosine, in mice and Syrian hamsters. Plasma kinetics and related metabolites were analyzed after a single dose. Tissue distribution was analyzed after repeated administration in drinking water. The compounds were quantified using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. In mice, homocarnosine and 2-oxo-homocarnosine maintained longer plasma exposure than carnosine. In hamsters, which have circulating CN1 activity, carnosine administration increased β-alanine, indicating rapid hydrolysis. Conversely, intact 2-oxo-carnosine and 2-oxo-homocarnosine were detected after the administration. Repeated administration of mixtures containing 2-oxo-carnosine or 2-oxo-homocarnosine resulted in elevated concentrations in various tissues, with particularly notable increases in the kidney and significant accumulation in the brain. Orally administered 2-oxo-IDPs demonstrated enhanced metabolic stability, allowing them to reach the brain and kidneys intact. These properties highlight their potential as bioactive compounds derived from food.
